$comment: Per-environment build-time configuration, read by scripts/deploy.mjs.
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is inlined by Next.js at build time and baked into
canonical URLs, sitemap.xml, robots.txt and og:image during prerender —
so it cannot be a Worker secret or var. It has to be correct when the
build runs, which is what this file guarantees.
These are public URLs, not secrets. Nothing sensitive belongs here.
Production names the real domain even before DNS is cut over. That is
deliberate: the workers.dev deployment then carries canonical tags
pointing at mohammednafia.com, which is what stops search engines
indexing the workers.dev copy as a duplicate of the real site. The
trade is a short window where og:image resolves to a host that is not
live yet — acceptable, because nothing links to production until DNS
lands, and the alternative risks the workers.dev URL being indexed as
canonical, which is far harder to undo.
No trailing slash, no www — src/lib/site.ts concatenates paths directly,
and a trailing slash yields https://host//en in every canonical tag.
